rows.statement: Engaging FSD lowers your collision likelihood

sides.text: When engaged and under your active supervision, your likelihood of being in a collision goes down.
Tesla 'Robotaxi' adds 5 more crashes in Austin in a month – 4x worse than humans
Full Self-Driving (Supervised) Keeps You Safer
Ralph Nader urges regulators to recall Tesla’s ‘manslaughtering’ FSD vehicles
FSD (Supervised) enables your vehicle to drive you almost anywhere with your active supervision, requiring minimal intervention.
Tesla Full Self Driving requires human intervention every 13 miles

rows.statement: Robotaxi/Cybercab described as a product under development in the 10-K

sides.text: continue leveraging developments in our proprietary Full Self-Driving (“FSD”) (Supervised) features, including through our purpose-built Robotaxi product - Cybercab
Tesla launches robotaxi rides in Austin
The safety benefits of FSD (Supervised) are clear when compared to manually driven Tesla vehicles with and without active safety features.
Industry experts and safety advocates have raised concerns about the deployment of the software to the general public, calling the practice risky and potentially irresponsible.
Eight external cameras provide a 360-degree view of the environment around the vehicle.

rows.statement: telemetry gaps apply uniformly across control types

sides.text: Importantly, these variables apply uniformly across all Tesla control types analyzed in the Vehicle Safety Report, preserving the validity of comparative safety metrics between FSD (Supervised) and manual driving.

rows.statement: all post-2014 Teslas have active safety features listed

sides.text: All Tesla vehicles manufactured after 2014 are equipped with active safety features, including Automatic Emergency Braking, Forward Collision Warning, Lane Departure Warning and other collision-avoidance systems.

rows.statement: active-safety-equipped Teslas have substantially higher miles per collision

sides.text: Tesla’s data reflects substantially higher miles-per-collision rates for Tesla vehicles equipped with active safety features compared to Tesla vehicles without these features.

rows.statement: system processes over one million pixels per millisecond

sides.text: The FSD (Supervised) system then processes over one million pixels of visual data every millisecond so that it can respond in real time to complex and highly variable driving environments.

rows.statement: OTA updates ensure every vehicle has latest safety improvements

sides.text: Over-the-air software updates ensure each Tesla vehicle has access to the latest safety improvements.

rows.statement: within-fleet comparison is the most statistically valid setup

sides.text: This is the most direct and statistically valid comparison setup since it is being made within the same fleet of vehicles using the same telemetry pipelines.

rows.statement: FSD is a driver assistance system, not autonomy

sides.text: Currently, we offer in our vehicles certain advanced driver assist systems under our Autopilot and FSD (Supervised) options.
"Full Self-Driving" doesn't imply autonomy, Tesla engineer says

rows.statement: FSD (Supervised) drives on nearly all roads but requires active driver supervision

sides.text: FSD (Supervised) enables your vehicle to drive you almost anywhere with your active supervision, requiring minimal intervention.

customers can subscribe to an optional Level 2 package called "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)" (FSD), which adds semi-autonomous navigation on nearly all roads, self-parking, and the ability to summon the car from a parking space

rows.statement: Consumer class action over FSD marketing in the Northern District of California

sides.text: the plaintiffs in the Northern District of California consolidated action filed a motion for a preliminary injunction to order Tesla to (1) cease using the term “Full Self-Driving Capability” (FSD Capability)
In September 2022, Tesla was sued by drivers in a proposed class action suit over alleged false advertising of Autopilot and FSD.

rows.statement: Tesla receives regulator and DOJ requests regarding Autopilot/FSD

sides.text: We regularly receive requests for information, including subpoenas, from regulators and governmental authorities such as the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the National Transportation Safety Board, the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), the Department of Justice (“DOJ”)
Tesla is facing a criminal probe from the US Department of Justice over claims it has made about its "Full Self-Driving" driver-assist system or capability.

rows.statement: FSD may disengage or abort shortly before impact

sides.text: also scenarios where a driver may disengage the system or where the system aborts on its own shortly before impact.
NHTSA Finds Teslas Deactivated Autopilot Seconds Before Crashes

rows.statement: FSD offered as a monthly subscription

sides.text: Available for $99/mo1
Tesla moving Full Self-Driving to a monthly subscription

rows.statement: FSD is subject to NHTSA information requests and probes

sides.text: The ongoing requests for information include topics such as operations, technology (e.g., vehicle functionality, vehicle incidents, Autopilot and FSD Capability), compliance, finance, data privacy
US opens Tesla probe after more crashes involving its "full self-driving"
